props.description: Explore the decisions behind competition robot design: movement, mechanisms, and sensing.

props.title: A robot is a series of decisions.
props.description: Explore the questions behind a competition robot: how it moves, handles objects, and senses the field. These are design concepts, not specifications for a particular team robot.

props.title: How a robot moves
props.question: What makes a drive system easy to control?
props.summary: Wheel choice, weight distribution, and motor control all affect how a robot crosses a field. A good design begins with the motion the game requires.

steps.text: Sketch the paths the robot needs to take.

props.title: How a robot handles objects
props.question: Can one mechanism do the job reliably?
props.summary: Intakes, lifts, and arms make game tasks possible. Their design balances reach, speed, strength, and the space available on the robot.

steps.text: Define the object and its destination.
Test jams and recovery before adding complexity.

props.title: How a robot knows where it is
props.question: What can the robot actually measure?
props.summary: Encoders, cameras, and other sensors give control code information about motion and surroundings. Each reading has uncertainty.

steps.text: Choose a measurement relevant to the task.
Compare the reading with what happens on the field.

props.text: Robot profiles can be added when photos, build notes, and specifications are ready to publish. The concepts above are a starting point for asking better engineering questions.
